note: Item codes are the deposit's own column names: data/kay_2025.R selects starts_with('act_xxx_') from OSF uzrgk data_deidentified.csv (z28r4) and pivots with names kept (t2_ prefix stripped for wave 2), resp = raw + 4. Wording transcribed verbatim from the study's own Qualtrics printouts on the same OSF node, 'Qualtrics Survey (Time 1).pdf' (au83k, blocks page_1 and page_2) and '(Time 2).pdf' (q9m27, page_1), which print each statement immediately followed by its export tag; T1 and T2 wording is identical apart from line wrapping. The T1 printout tags items 3-4 as '(acts_xxx_03_x)'/'(acts_xxx_04_x)' while the deposit column, the T2 printout and the authors' own processing Rmd (5a3gc, matches('^act_'), no rename) all use act_; treated as a display-label typo, content and position agree. Curly quotes around 'run' kept as printed. Instructions are the block stem 'Please indicate your level of agreement with each of the statements below.' shared with the other scales in the same mixed block. Anchors printed as Strongly disagree (-3), Moderately disagree (-2), Slightly disagree (-1), Neither agree nor disagree (0), Slightly agree (1), Moderately agree (2), Strongly agree (3); deposit act columns span -3..3, none is an _r column (authors reverse only _r$), so IRW 1..7 = those anchors in order. Every item uses all 7 levels in both waves. Rights: instrument_rights_register.csv ACTS row, verdict ship (Ben 2026-09-23, irw#2381 R12, origin Klofstad et al. 2019 CC BY), applied not re-derived.

source_ref: Goksel, Sezer & Berman (2026), JPSP 130(6), doi:10.1037/pspa0000477; OSF deposit osf.io/jwdq6 (dictionary licence as for the shipped siblings): Codebook_Transcending Embarrassment.xlsx sheets Study 2/4/6 (https://osf.io/download/p9yn4/, sha256 5df77811c2ececbc...), Study 2 Qualtrics.pdf (https://osf.io/download/cv9hu/, sha256 7b02470f7f9f21ea...), Study 4 Qualtrics.pdf (https://osf.io/download/ubt3f/, sha256 b88d932811b1d4ed...), Study 6 Qualtrics.pdf (https://osf.io/download/sc38x/, sha256 96ed613231604d2e...), Study2/4/6 Cleaned Data.xls (https://osf.io/download/35fv7/, /pjx4d/, /mgufs/; sha256 c4a9eace54bb7593..., e3720c49116055a3..., 0e00300bb43a1448...)
note: Code derivation: item IS the source column name lowercased (WCM_1..12 in Study2/4/6 Cleaned Data.xls; data/goksel_2026_embarrassment.py melts s2, s4, s6 via _cols('WCM', 12) with an identity rename then str.lower). The deposit codebook labels each column identically on the Study 2, Study 4 and Study 6 sheets: ratings on the item "competent", "intelligent", "skillful", "capable", "warm", "extraverted", "friendly", "sociable", "sincere", "trustworthy", "moral", "honest" (12/12 on each of the 3 sheets). All three Qualtrics prints show the same 12 adjectives in a different, study-specific order (e.g. Study 2: honest, competent, intelligent, warm, moral, ...), so print order was NOT used for the mapping. Cross-checks: each cleaned file's avg_competence / avg_warmth / avg_moral(ity) equals the row mean of WCM_1-4 / 5-8 / 9-12 (max abs diff 0.0 in all 9 study x subscale checks), consistent with the codebook's adjective grouping; live n per study (s2 399, s4 299, s6 802) and the pooled item x resp counts equal the three cleaned files in 60/60 cells (e.g. wcm_1 32/157/535/569/207, wcm_6 83/256/322/494/345). Options: codebook value labels (-2) = strongly disagree, 0 = neither agree nor disagree, 2 = strongly agree; prints show 'Strongly disagree (-2)', '(-1)', 'Neither agree nor disagree (0)', '(1)', 'Strongly agree (2)'; raw exports and cleaned files store 1..5, so resp 1..5 = those columns in order; anchors shipped without the parenthetical -2..2 values, points 2 and 4 unlabelled and left blank. Instructions transcribed from the Study 2 print with ${e://Field/name} rendered [name], as in the sibling goksel tables; Study 6 pipes ${e://Field/actor} and Study 4 reads 'this person' instead (disclosed in public_note). Deviation: the Study 4 print spells item 10 'trstworthy'; shipped 'trustworthy' per the codebook and the Study 2 and 6 prints. Rights: single trait adjectives from the study's own materials, no instrument rights holder and no restriction located.
public_note: The instructions name the rated person as [name] (Study 2); Study 6 respondents read the piped actor name in that position and Study 4 respondents read 'this person', and the three studies presented the 12 adjectives in different orders.

source_ref: Ren X-Q et al. (2024) Sci Rep 14:14057, doi:10.1038/s41598-024-65095-0 (CC BY 4.0), Methods 'Three-item loneliness scale' and Table 2; data 41598_2024_65095_MOESM2_ESM.sav variable labels L1-L3 (also MOESM3_ESM.xlsx sheet 'Data', MOESM1_ESM.docx checked); processing script data/ren_2024_rural_elderly.py; middle anchor from Hughes ME, Waite LJ, Hawkley LC, Cacioppo JT (2004) Res Aging 26:655-672
note: Item codes ARE the source column names (data/ren_2024_rural_elderly.py melts L1..L3 unchanged, only dropping out-of-range values). Mapping from the deposit .sav's own variable labels (41598_2024_65095_MOESM2_ESM.sav, sha256 4e54006c4a6c3a7cdf5977c5013447f5d3e2b057297d979fa05de68026703b5c): L1='I feel left out', L2='I feel isolated', L3='I lack companionship', 3/3; no value labels. The paper's Methods quotes the same three strings in the same order. Note this is NOT Hughes et al. (2004) canonical order (lack companionship / left out / isolated), so canonical numbering must not be applied to these codes; the labels govern. Live per-item counts match the .sav cell for cell (L1 1169/257/161, L2 1260/227/100, L3 1356/156/75 at resp 1/2/3). item_text = the .sav labels verbatim (terse first-person study renderings, not Hughes's 'How often do you feel...' questions). Option axis: paper states '1 (hardly ever) ~ 3 (often)', total 3-9; live sum over 1587 complete respondents M 3.827 SD 1.561 vs Table 2 Loneliness 3.83/1.56 (reversed would give 8.17), so resp 1 = hardly ever. The paper labels only the endpoints; the middle anchor 'Some of the time' is from the canonical Hughes et al. (2004) three-item scale, and endpoints are given in Hughes's capitalisation ('Hardly ever','Often') where the paper prints them lower-case in parentheses. Administered language: household survey of 1,587 rural older adults in China, Chinese version per Liu et al.; no Chinese wording in the deposit or supplements (.sav: 0 CJK across 83 variable/value labels; MOESM3 xlsx bare headers; MOESM1 docx English-only, as checked for sibling ren_2024_phq9 in batch_320). Fallback: English in base fields, language=Chinese, _translated empty. translation_source=mixed: item_text is study_supplied (.sav labels/paper), option_text is official_instrument_english (Hughes 2004) for the middle anchor and capitalisation. Instructions left blank: the study publishes none (only that the recall frame was the past week). Rights: instrument_rights_register.csv UCLA-L row verdict=ship, applied (Hughes three-item scale is a short form of the R-UCLA; reinwarth_2023_loneliness3 precedent).
public_note: Respondents answered a Chinese-language version; the item text shown is the study's own short English rendering from its data file, and only the end anchors were published by the study, so 'Some of the time' is the standard wording of the three-item scale.
